prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "proof", with the standing line "Holds each scanned page's extracted words against a picture of the original, mending only the scanner's mistakes and never the author's." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows On the left sits a tall stack of text pages from extracted.md, each page topped by its page marker. On the right sits the bound book.pdf, and one sheet slides out through pdftoppm, which renders it as a crisp page image. The single page's extracted text and its page image are laid side by side and enter the vision model together. The arrows run one way: the text comes from the stack, the image comes from pdftoppm, and both converge on the model. From the model, one corrected page emerges, headed again by its page marker. It drops down toward and rejoins the other pages in order.

Magnified circles set beside it show The first circle shows the long-s ſ misread as f, now restored to s. The second shows a broken ligature, with two letters mended into one word. The third shows a word split at a line end, now rejoined. The fourth shows "colour" and "connexion" left untouched, the author's spelling protected. The row of small studies holds four scenes. In the first, a nearly empty page under 40 characters passes by uncorrected. In the second, a failed render and an API error each return the original text beside a warning. In the third, a dry run lists pages with no model call. In the fourth, start page and end page brackets mark a run on a stretch of the book.

Colour is used so that : Vermilion marks each repair of scanning damage. Slate blue marks the author's original spelling, grammar and punctuation that must stand. Amber marks a doubtful correction left for a human.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: S: 200 DPI, shown as a dimension mark on the rendered page image. 40 characters, marked as the threshold on the near-empty page. Two inputs and one output, counted at the model's entry and exit. Four kinds of fix against four kinds of protected writing, counted down the circles. One page per model call.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: Y: extracted.md sits on the stack of text pages. book.pdf sits on the bound original. The page marker heads each page block. pdftoppm sits on the rendering step. The page image sits on the rendered sheet. --text-model sits on the vision model. The long-s (ſ) sits in the first circle. The broken ligature sits in the second circle. The rejoined word sits in the third circle. "colour" and "connexion" sit on the protected spelling. The dry run sits on the listing study. The start page and end page sit on the range brackets. proofed.md sits on the finished file. "uncertain: old → new" sits on the amber-flagged correction. The cost ledger and total cost sit on the ledger book.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: : extracted.md, book.pdf, page marker, pdftoppm, page image, extracted text, vision model, --text-model. long-s misread, ſ becomes s, broken ligature, rejoined word, colour stands. under 40 characters, render failed, API error, original kept, dry run, start page, end page. proofed.md, uncertain: old → new, cost ledger, total cost. split pages, render, compare, correct, reassemble.

Set these short notes beside what they explain: S: Every page checked against its own picture; Text and image travel together. Fix only scanning damage; Change nothing the author wrote. Skipped pages pass through untouched; A warning prints, the text is kept. Doubtful corrections wait for a human; Every call lands in the ledger.
